openings.claim: Hypothesis: a clearance-rich shared plywood cradle restores the pointer through repeatable seating rather than matched rod width. Seat each rod against its insertion stop, then the same two adjacent datum faces, then hand-tighten bolt restraint; elastic loops bias seating and cord captures releasable hardware.
openings.discriminator: Against opposed symmetric tightening using identical hardware, datum-first seating predicts smaller post-exchange error, including 18 mm substitution. Better return with greater loaded drift leaves restraint unresolved. Two supplied trials suggest this discriminator; they establish no success.
openings.probe: Fabricate one captive cradle within 100 minutes using the six plywood pieces, eight bolts/nuts, four washers, loops, cord and permitted tools; cut/drill only plywood. Before exchanges verify the 90 mm cube envelope and captive loosened hardware. Within 20 testing minutes compare two configurations, counterbalancing order. Each receives twelve exchanges: five per original rod, then two 18 mm substitutions; and four 10 N lateral-load trials lasting ten seconds. Log return, loaded displacement, exchange time and retention. Stop on retention failure; stopped trials establish no success.
openings.uncertainty: Rod orientation is unspecified. Datum rigidity, adequate restraint, unobstructed secure cord retention, non-indenting preload and available measurement resolution remain unproved. Worse return than the rival, target escape under load, any exchange reaching forty seconds, loose components or exhausted time defeats success; incomplete trials remain unresolved.

lineage.reason: Preserves the seating mechanism, rival, bounded probe and unresolved dependencies.

decision: Retain for an enabling experiment. Require return within the 2 mm target circle and continued containment under load, exchanges under forty seconds, hand-only assembly/adjustment, no drilling, adhesive or permanent rod marks, and no falling components. Neither repeatability nor load resistance is demonstrated.
